question.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ If ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-7{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=4{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1},$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C.$

current_example.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2\}$ and $\mathcal{C}=\{\mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2\}$ be bases of $\mathbb{R}^2.$ If $\mathbf{c}_1=\mathbf{b}_2-4\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{c}_2=5\mathbf{b}_1+7\mathbf{b}_2,$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$
